data.title: The Night Ferry
data.rumour: The island ferry makes a run at two in the morning. It isn't on the timetable.

nfBird.name: Carved stone cormorant
tells: Black soapstone, wings half open, drying itself the way they do on the pilings.
Under the base, half scrubbed away, a number painted in white: 1931.44. That is a museum's number.

nfJam.name: Beach plum jam, 1786
tells: A squat green jar, waxed and tied with linen. Inside, something dark that was plums once.
The paper label, in iron-gall ink: "Beach Plum. Gannet. Sept. 1786. M.H." It has never been opened.

nfTag.name: Museum accession tag
tells: A small card tag with a brass rim. It came off a piece on the two o'clock boat.

nfPiece.name: Crated museum piece
tells: Packed in straw, with a museum's number on it. It belongs on a shelf with a little card under it.

about: A smuggling story. Roz Teague, a deckhand on the island ferry, pawns a carved stone cormorant she says was left aboard (§{rozBird}). Then she tells you about the run at two in the morning that isn't on the timetable: crates of "marine parts", every item tagged from a museum collection, and a jar of 1786 beach plum jam loose in the straw (§{rozJar}). Get her to take you aboard, or keep the tag and stay out of it (Missed the Boat).

On the two o'clock ferry (§{nfDeck}) a launch with no lights swaps crates in the dark, and a man in a long coat counts them. Roz brings you the tags she's kept (§{rozTags}). On Gannet's back dock (§{nfDock}) the man turns out to be Merrit Gaunt of the Gilded Hand: the Hand repossesses island houses and sells on what was never theirs to pledge. He offers you an envelope to store things for a week. Odile said no to him once.

Tess, the harbormaster, wants to know why you've been on her water at two in the morning (§{nfShack}). Put two or more museum tags on her desk and the ferry is shut down (Lit Up). Post the pieces back to the museums anonymously (Return to Sender). Or say you were fishing, and keep taking envelopes if you took one (Riding Along). Roz quits and sells you what was left loose in the last crate (§{rozOut}), and Bettany would pay $240 for the 1786 jam (§{nfBettany}).
data.notes: Each piece on the night boat carries a museum tag, from a collection somebody emptied: the Athenaeum, Fall River and the Commonwealth. Who runs it: Merrit Gaunt, the Gilded Hand's collector.

rozBird.title: Roz Teague pawns a stone cormorant with a museum number

text: Roz Teague. I work the island ferry. Deckhand, ropes, tickets, sick bags.
Somebody left this aboard. Nobody's claimed it, so it's salvage, right? That's how salvage works.

text.then: If anyone asks, I found it on the night run. No. I found it on the day run. There's no night run.
text.else: Fine. I'll throw it over the side. That's what they'd want. Probably.

rozJar.title: Roz tells you about the two o'clock boat

text: Me again. I need to tell somebody, and you're the only one in town who looks at things for a living.
Two nights a week the ferry goes out at two in the morning. Not on the timetable. No passengers. Just crates, MARINE PARTS. They pay me two hundred a run to tie up and not look.
I looked. Everything in those crates has one of these on it.

steps.narrate: She puts a little brass-rimmed tag on the counter. HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.117.

steps.text: And this was loose in the straw. It's jam. It's jam from 1786. Who ships jam at two in the morning?

add.name: Athenaeum tag
tells: A museum tag, brass-rimmed: HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.117. "Gift of Capt. J. Hale."

else.toast: No room on your shelves: athenaeum tag stays with Roz.

then.text: {placed:nf-deck}, quarter to two, the town slip. Wear something dark. If the skipper asks, you're my cousin and you get seasick.

choose.label: Take the tag, and stay out of it

add.name: Athenaeum tag
tells: A museum tag, brass-rimmed: HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.117. "Gift of Capt. J. Hale."

else.toast: No room on your shelves: athenaeum tag stays with Roz.

then.text: Keep it, then. If something happens to me, at least somebody's got a tag.
Nobody's boat. That's the whole trouble.

nfDeck.title: The ferry at two in the morning

steps.narrate: The island ferry, two in the morning, running without her deck lights. Nobody in the wheelhouse says a word. The skipper is a shape in a cap behind the glass.

steps.text: Behind the life jackets. If anyone comes aft, you're sick.

steps.narrate: Halfway across, the engine drops to an idle. Out of the dark a launch comes alongside, no running lights, and somebody hands a crate across and takes one back.

choose.label: Get a look inside a crate

then.narrate: The lid is only tacked down. Straw, and a ship's decanter with a little card tied to its neck. You slip the card into your pocket and press the lid back.

add.name: Fall River tag
tells: A museum tag: FALL RIVER MARINE COLLECTION, 1958.22. The string has been cut, not untied.

else.toast: No room on your shelves: fall river tag stays with Roz.

then.narrate: From the launch, a polite voice: "One of the lids is up, Roz." Then the launch is gone.

then.text: He counts lids. He counts everything.

choose.label: Stay behind the life jackets and watch the launch

then.narrate: On the launch, a man in a long coat stands very still, with the light catching a pair of glasses. He checks each crate against a clipboard and doesn't once look at the sea.

then.text: Never says his name. Says thank you. Every time. That's the worst part.

steps.narrate: On the way back you pass the harbormaster's shack. A light is on. A pair of binoculars catches the moon. Somebody has been watching this boat for a long time.

steps.text: Thursday next week is the big run. He comes to the island himself to sign for it. The old coal dock, round the back of Gannet.

steps.toast: Calendar: Gannet Island's back dock, next week

rozTags.title: Roz brings the tags she's kept

text: He knew. Someone had been aboard. He asked me, very nicely, if I had a cousin. I said I have six. I do have six.
I've been keeping these. One off every crate I could. I want them somewhere that isn't my locker.

steps.text: One crate said LUSK on the side. Crowns of the Stage, the label said. So that's where that was going.

add.name: Commonwealth tag
tells: A museum tag: COMMONWEALTH MARITIME MUSEUM, 1931.44. Somebody tried to rub the number off with a thumb.

else.toast: No room on your shelves: commonwealth tag stays with Roz.

then.text: Thank you. I feel lighter. I feel about a tag lighter.
You burn them. I can't. My hands won't.

nfDock.title: Who signs for the crates, on Gannet's back dock

narrate: The old coal dock round the back of Gannet Island, two in the morning. A bulb burns in the boathouse. Crates wait on a hand truck. Out on the black water, the launch idles with no lights.
A man in a long coat steps off it onto the ladder, clipboard first.

steps.text: Good evening. Or good morning. I never know which, at this hour.

steps.note: now you know who he is

text: Keeper. Of course it's you. Your aunt used to stand exactly there, a long time ago, before she lost her nerve.
The Hand repossesses. Island houses, mostly. And what's in the houses. Some of what we take was never theirs to pledge: a museum's, a library's. Nobody has missed it in a hundred years.
It goes out on the night boat to people who will miss it very much indeed, and pay accordingly. You have a shop. Shops are wonderful places to keep things for a week.

steps.narrate: He holds out an envelope. It is thick.

then.text: Splendid. You'll find it's very quiet work. Nobody ever asks a pawnshop where something came from. You've made sure of that yourself.

choose.label: Take it, and keep every tag you can

then.text: Splendid. You'll find it's very quiet work. Nobody ever asks a pawnshop where something came from. You've made sure of that yourself.
No. Odile said no, too. Well. It's a long month, keeper, and the installments don't pay themselves.

then.narrate: While he signs for the crates, Roz bumps the hand truck. A tag comes loose and lands by your boot. You put your foot on it.

then.note: one of the three tags, at random

add.name: Athenaeum tag
tells: A museum tag, brass-rimmed: HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.117. "Gift of Capt. J. Hale."

else.toast: No room on your shelves: athenaeum tag stays with Roz.

add.name: Fall River tag
tells: A museum tag: FALL RIVER MARINE COLLECTION, 1958.22. The string has been cut, not untied.

else.toast: No room on your shelves: fall river tag stays with Roz.

add.name: Commonwealth tag
tells: A museum tag: COMMONWEALTH MARITIME MUSEUM, 1931.44. Somebody tried to rub the number off with a thumb.

else.toast: No room on your shelves: commonwealth tag stays with Roz.

steps.text: I'm done after this. I'm done. I'm saying it out loud so it counts.

steps.toast: Calendar: the harbormaster's shack, after dark

rozOut.title: Roz gets out, and sells what was loose in the last crate

text: I quit. Handed in my ticket punch. The skipper didn't even look up.
I took what was left loose in the last crate. I want it gone, and I want it to go somewhere good. I don't know where good is. You might.

offer.name: Scrimshaw busk, crated
tells: A whalebone corset busk, carved with a ship and two initials. A tag: HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.120.

text.then: There. It's yours. I'm going to go and stand in a field.
text.else: Then it goes in the harbor. Maybe the fish will put it in a little case.

nfShack.title: Tess has questions, at the harbormaster's shack

steps.narrate: The harbormaster's shack, after dark. The ferry's logbook is open on the desk. Two in the morning is written nowhere in it.

steps.text: You've been out on my water at two in the morning. Twice. I'd like to know why, before I decide what to think about you.
I've watched that ferry since 1991. Boats that go out with no lights, I take personally.

choose.label: Lay the museum tags on her desk

then.text: Athenaeum. Fall River. Commonwealth. That's not smuggling, that's a library card.

then.narrate: On Thursday Tess and two state troopers are on the town slip at a quarter to two. The ferry doesn't leave. The launch does, very fast, and is found next morning tied up at the Gilded Hand's own mooring.

then.text: And the envelope he gave you, you'll give that to the church roof. I'm not asking.

then.with: Merrit's envelope, to the Saint Brine's roof
then.note: up to $150, as much as you have

then.narrate: Merrit Gaunt's name is never in the paper. A shell company called Gannet Coal is fined a great deal. On Monday he collects your installment without a word, and counts the bills twice.

then.why: Shut down the two o'clock ferry

choose.label: Post the pieces home, one parcel at a time

text: You want to post them back. With no name on the parcel. To museums.
I didn't hear that. I'll lend you my packing tape. I didn't lend you that either.

narrate.then: For a week, a parcel goes out of the Hollow Neck post office every Tuesday with no return address. A curator in Fall River writes to the paper about it. She calls you "a friend of the collection."
narrate.else: For {loot.count} weeks, a parcel goes out of the Hollow Neck post office every Tuesday with no return address. A curator in Fall River writes to the paper about it. She calls you "a friend of the collection."

then.text: Fishing. At two in the morning. On a ferry.

then.narrate: She looks at you, then at the logbook, and closes it.
On the way home there's a parcel on your step: a crate of MARINE PARTS to keep for a week, and another envelope.

text: Is that... in the green jar. Is that beach plum? Off Gannet? I can see the wax from the door.
I've been trying to make beach plum the old way for twenty years. Nobody writes it down. That jar is a recipe with a lid on.

then.why: Sold the 1786 jam to Bettany Lowe

then.text: I'm not going to eat it. I'm going to smell it once, at Christmas, and cry.
If it's ever unspoken for. Twenty years. I can wait another week.

add.name: Athenaeum tag
tells: A museum tag, brass-rimmed: HOLLOW NECK ATHENAEUM, 1902.117. "Gift of Capt. J. Hale."

add.name: Fall River tag
tells: A museum tag: FALL RIVER MARINE COLLECTION, 1958.22. The string has been cut, not untied.

epilogue.line: The two o'clock ferry is a timetable joke now. Roz Teague works at the Athenaeum, cataloging everything twice.
Three museums have a new card in a case: "Returned anonymously, Hollow Neck." Nobody in Hollow Neck says a word.
Some weeks a crate of MARINE PARTS sits in your back room for a night. You never open it. You count the envelope instead.
